title: Interaction ledger endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/interactions x-module P3; TSD v5 P3 API-P3-014 and API-P3-015
description: The API Specification v4 (x-module P3) and TSD v5 P3 (API-P3-014, API-P3-015) put GET and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions in rwb-case; the plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling puts the interaction ledger in rwb-source-data (P1). The owner is set to P1 by the default ruling; rwb-case reads the ledger through the P1 contract.
evidence: API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/interactions x-module P3; TSD v5 P3 API-P3-014 and API-P3-015
proposed: Confirm the interaction ledger owner; if P1, rwb-case reads interactions through a P1 contract and does not write the ledger

title: Feature flag endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /feature-flags and /admin/feature-flags x-module P2; TSD v5 P2 API-P2-005 to API-P2-008
description: API Specification v4 x-module P2 and TSD v5 P2 (API-P2-005 to API-P2-008) put the four feature-flag paths in rwb-integration; the plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling makes feature flags a platform library. The owner is set to PLT.
evidence: API Specification v4 /feature-flags and /admin/feature-flags x-module P2; TSD v5 P2 API-P2-005 to API-P2-008
proposed: Confirm the feature flag library and its owning platform epic (RWB-PLT-LIB)

title: Rule package registry endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /admin/rule-package* x-module P3; API Specification v2 and v3 /admin/rule-versions x-module P4; TSD v5 P3 and P4 appendices T-A
description: The seven /admin/rule-package* paths are x-module P3 in API Specification v4 and are claimed by both TSD v5 P3 (API-P3-020 to API-P3-026) and TSD v5 P4 (API-P4-014 to API-P4-020); the four /admin/rule-versions paths are x-module P4 in v2 and v3. Arch v5 slide 14 gives rwb-decision the DMN model registry and the plan default ruling gives it the rule package registry, so all eleven paths are owned by P7.
evidence: API Specification v4 /admin/rule-package* x-module P3; API Specification v2 and v3 /admin/rule-versions x-module P4; TSD v5 P3 and P4 appendices T-A
proposed: Confirm that rwb-decision owns the rule package registry and that rwb-case and rwb-access hold no rule package administration

title: Reference data endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /admin/lists and /admin/reference-loads x-module P4; TSD v5 P4 API-P4-004 to API-P4-010
description: API Specification v4 x-module P4 and TSD v5 P4 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-010) put GET /admin/lists/{listCode} and the four /admin/reference-loads* paths in rwb-access; Arch v5 slide 14 calls rwb-access the reference data owner. The plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling puts parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) in rwb-case, so the five paths are owned by P3; the role, DoA and template endpoints stay with the services named in Arch v5 slide 41.
evidence: API Specification v4 /admin/lists and /admin/reference-loads x-module P4; TSD v5 P4 API-P4-004 to API-P4-010
proposed: Confirm the reference data service owner and the split from the access service

title: Platform smoke endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /admin/workflows/smoke x-module P3; TSD v5 P3 API-P3-027 and P4 API-P4-021; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22
description: API Specification v4 x-module P3, TSD v5 P3 (API-P3-027) and TSD v5 P4 (API-P4-021) put POST /admin/workflows/smoke in a service; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22 and Batch and Scheduling Design v4 run PlatformSmokeWorkflow on task queue rwb-platform with the platform administrator. The owner is set to PLT.
evidence: API Specification v4 /admin/workflows/smoke x-module P3; TSD v5 P3 API-P3-027 and P4 API-P4-021; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22
proposed: Confirm that the smoke trigger is exposed by the platform, not by rwb-case

title: Asset valuation endpoint ownership
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: API Specification v4 /assets/{assetKey}/valuations x-module S5; TSD v5 S5 API-S5-003; TSD v5 S1 T3.1; Arch v5 slide 41
description: API Specification v4 x-module S5 and TSD v5 S5 (API-S5-003) put POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations in rwb-asset; TSD v5 S1 T3.1 owns the valuation table (DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-044) and Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-valuation the valuations. The owner is set to S1.
evidence: API Specification v4 /assets/{assetKey}/valuations x-module S5; TSD v5 S5 API-S5-003; TSD v5 S1 T3.1; Arch v5 slide 41
proposed: Confirm that rwb-asset calls rwb-valuation to record a valuation and writes no valuation row

title: TimerDue event retired but still listed with an owner
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Arch v5 slide 42 row 18; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events sheet EV-18
description: Arch v5 slide 42 row 18 gives TimerDue the producer "durable timer" and marks it retired (timer inside the workflow); Event and Messaging Design v4 gives the owning module "Case and workflow". The owner is set to P3, the service that hosts the case timers and still publishes TimerBreached (EV-19).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 18; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events sheet EV-18
proposed: Confirm that TimerDue is retired and that no service publishes it in the target

title: COLLINS load check job retired but still in the job list
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-01; Arch v5 slide 44
description: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 marks JOB-01 retired under D-RCV-35 with the ACE team as owner; Arch v5 slide 44 omits it. The owner is set to P1, the successor read path through the recovery.v_ace_* views and the AceIngestCheck workflow.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-01; Arch v5 slide 44
proposed: Confirm that no Workbench job replaces JOB-01 and that rwb-source-data carries the read path

title: Timer check job has no single owner and is retired
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-05; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-05
description: Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-05 the owner "all" and the mechanism "durable timers (retired)"; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 names the platform administrator. A single owner is set to PLT for the shared timer capability.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-05; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-05
proposed: Confirm that durable timers replace the five-minute timer check and that PLT owns the timer library

title: File load job retired but still in the job list
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-09; Arch v5 slide 44
description: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 marks JOB-09 retired under D-RCV-35 with the ACE team as owner; Arch v5 slide 44 omits it. The owner is set to P1, the successor read path through the recovery.v_ace_* views.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-09; Arch v5 slide 44
proposed: Confirm that no Workbench job replaces JOB-09 and that rwb-source-data carries the read path

title: WIN notice job names two owners
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-10; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-10
description: Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-10 the owner "rwb-comms + integration"; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 names the platform administrator. The owner is set to P6, which writes the daily notice file and calls rwb-integration deliverFile.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-10; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-10
proposed: Confirm that rwb-comms owns the WIN file and rwb-integration only delivers it

title: Outbox sender runs in every service
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-11; Arch v5 slide 20 (every service template); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-11
description: Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-11 the owner "every service" and the mechanism "outbox relay to Kafka"; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 names the platform administrator. The owner is set to PLT for the relay that comes with the service template (Arch v5 slide 20).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-11; Arch v5 slide 20 (every service template); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-11
proposed: Confirm that the outbox relay is a platform library and that no service builds its own

title: Decision log copy to the data lake disagrees with Arch v5
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-13; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13; Arch v5 slide 14 (daily ledger seal, WORM)
description: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 copies the decision log to the data lake nightly at 01:00; Arch v5 slide 44 says the ingest is continuous over Kafka and Arch v5 names no data lake, with the daily ledger seal in rwb-decision (slide 14). The owner is set to P7 and the replacement to the daily ledger seal.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-13; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13; Arch v5 slide 14 (daily ledger seal, WORM)
proposed: Confirm the daily ledger seal replaces the data lake copy and that no data lake remains in scope

title: Reporting extract to the data lake disagrees with Arch v5
source: Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 and API Specification v4
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-15; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-15; Arch v5 slide 15 (rwb-reporting OUT)
description: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 writes the reporting extract to the data lake nightly at 01:30; Arch v5 slide 44 replaces it with an Airflow trigger and names no data lake, and Arch v5 slide 15 sends the regulatory extract through rwb-integration. The owner is set to P9.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs sheet JOB-15; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-15; Arch v5 slide 15 (rwb-reporting OUT)
proposed: Confirm that the reporting extract is the regulatory extract and that no data lake remains in scope
